_comment: Lesson 1: ownership through pattern matching (Ch4 Understanding Ownership, Ch5 structs, Ch6 Enums and Pattern Matching). Lesson 2 (added 2026-08-31): Ch8 Common Collections (vectors, strings, hash maps), Ch9 Error Handling (panic!, Result, the ? operator - ch09-03 'to panic or not to panic' intentionally omitted, out of Lesson 2's stated scope), Ch10 Generic Types, Traits, and Lifetimes (all three sections: generic data types, traits, lifetimes). Ch10 traits coverage directly closes the known false-positive documented in _relevanceThresholdRationale below (the 'implement a custom trait' probe query, previously ungrounded and scoring 12.90).
_relevanceThresholdRationale: Re-checked 2026-08-31 after the pack grew from 7 to 15 chapters/sections (added Ch8 Collections, Ch9 Error Handling, Ch10 Generics/Traits/Lifetimes). This was a real re-check, not an assumption that 9.0 still holds: a 14-good/8-bad probe spanning every topic area (ownership/borrowing/slices, structs, enums/match/if-let, vectors/strings/hash maps, panic/Result/?, generics/traits/lifetimes) plus 8 bad queries (2 true off-topic controls - pasta carbonara, chess - and 6 Rust-adjacent-but-still-uncovered topics - closures/iterators ch13, smart pointers ch15, threads ch16, async/await, macros, unsafe) confirmed the fix and confirmed the threshold: 'how do I implement a custom trait for my struct' - the query that previously false-positived at 12.90 with no trait content indexed at all - now grounds at 12.72 citing ch10-02's 'Implementing a Trait on a Type', a real, correctly-grounded match, not a coincidence of vocabulary overlap. 9.0 (unchanged from the prior calibration) still separates this larger, more diverse corpus about as well as any single scalar can: 10 of 14 good queries ground correctly (scores 9.16-16.66), and 7 of 8 bad queries correctly refuse. The one confirmed residual false positive changed identity but not shape: 'how do I use closures and iterators in rust' (ch13, not indexed) now scores 13.15 - HIGHER than 3 of the pack's own good matches (reference-vs-ownership 12.40, custom-trait 12.72, add-to-vector 12.95) - because the retrieved chunk ('Returning Types That Implement Traits', ch10) shares heavy generic/trait vocabulary with the query. Blocking it would need a threshold above 13.15, which would also refuse 11 of the 14 good queries (everything except enum-with-data 15.49, the ?-operator 16.66, and multiple-immutable-refs 13.73) - tried and rejected as strictly worse. Also tried and rejected: 8.0 (adds 2 more false positives - smart-pointers 8.03, pasta 8.20 - for zero good-query gain) and 8.5 (gains nothing over 9.0 while thinning the margin against those same two bad queries from ~0.8-1.0 down to ~0.3-0.5). Confirmed residual false negatives: 4 good queries now refuse purely for sparse phrasing, not missing coverage - 'what does match do in rust' (3.93), 'what is a generic function in rust' (4.99), 'if let vs match' (5.96), 'how do lifetimes work in function signatures' (8.35) - all genuinely covered by ch06/ch10 but phrased too briefly to clear 9.0; a student hitting this would need to rephrase with more specific vocabulary. Net effect of the corpus growth: one prior false negative fixed for free ('struct vs tuple' now scores 10.38, up from below-threshold before, most likely from ch10's generic-data-types chunk sharpening the tuple-struct chunk's relative term weights), one prior false positive fixed by real content growth (the trait query, above), and the previous 12.90 outlier's role taken over by a new query on a still-uncovered topic - the underlying BM25 corpus-heterogeneity limitation persists at any usable threshold, same class as content-packs/firmware/manifest.json's RAM-budget case, and is not fully engineered away by threshold choice alone. See README's 'A real, honest limitation' section.
